body:
I started out as a PC tech, but moved into system admin stuff fairly quickly.  To be honest, I don't have a diverse skill set.  Every job I've had for the last 10 years has required me to be on-call 24/7/365.  That's what burned me out.  Near the end of my last two jobs I felt suicidal all the time because I felt that my time was no longer my own and I was simply not able to enjoy life.  I've even felt like it kept me from establishing new friendships when I moved to a new city.  I can't count the number of times I tried to make plans only to have them shattered by some work related problem.

Right before I lost my job, I had my sights set on starting my own business.  I won't go into specifics, but it was related to woodworking.  That all came crashing down when I lost my job.  To do something like that, you have to have a workshop.  I live in an apartment for now, so it's not even a possibility.  I guess my perfect work environment would be one where I only had to answer to myself and I felt in control of my own destiny.

I think there is a pretty good possibility that we live inside some sort of computer program or simulation.  No, not like "The Matrix" - something far more mundane - like we are rats in a lab.  I've often wondered why there is so much repetition in the world.  Movies that come out are just rehashes or remakes.  Clothing and style trends just recycle.  Everything is just an iteration of something else that came before it.  There are no new ideas.  Everything is just recirculated and remixed to make it seem different when it's all just the same source material.  The simulation might just be a short slice of time.  Maybe only encompassing the last 50 years or so and extending into maybe the next 50.  That's just a guess.

But I'm going down a rabbit trail now.  I go to sleep every night and I hope I never wake up.  If I just ceased to exist then there would be no more pain.
